authoredSolutions.1: For a spring-mass oscillator \(T = 2\pi\sqrt{m/k}\), so \(k = \dfrac{4\pi^{2}m}{T^{2}}\). Relative errors combine in magnitude (worst case): \[\frac{\Delta k}{k} = \frac{\Delta m}{m} + 2\,\frac{\Delta T}{T}.\] Hence the percentage error in \(k\) is \(1\% + 2(2\%) = 5\%\). The sign of an individual error never reduces the maximum possible error, so the correct choice is D.
authoredSolutions.2: Kinetic energy is \(K = \tfrac{1}{2}mv^{2}\), so the fractional loss depends only on the speeds: \[\frac{\Delta K}{K_{i}} = \frac{v_{i}^{2} - v_{f}^{2}}{v_{i}^{2}} = \frac{100^{2} - 40^{2}}{100^{2}} = \frac{10000 - 1600}{10000} = 0.84.\] The loss is \(84\%\), so the correct choice is D.
authoredSolutions.3: The series limit (shortest wavelength) has \(n_{2}\to\infty\), so \(\dfrac{1}{\lambda} = \dfrac{R}{n_{1}^{2}}\). For Balmer \(n_{1}=2\Rightarrow \lambda_{B} = 4/R\); for Lyman \(n_{1}=1\Rightarrow \lambda_{L} = 1/R\). Therefore \(\lambda_{B}:\lambda_{L} = 4:1\) and the correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.4: To reach infinity with zero final speed the kinetic energy must equal the magnitude of the gravitational potential energy at the surface: \[K = \frac{GM_{E}m}{R_{E}}.\] Since \(g = \dfrac{GM_{E}}{R_{E}^{2}}\), we get \(GM_{E} = gR_{E}^{2}\) and hence \(K = mgR_{E}\). The correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.5: In a medium \(v = \dfrac{c}{\sqrt{\mu_{r}\varepsilon_{r}}}\), so \[\mu_{r}\varepsilon_{r} = \frac{c^{2}}{v^{2}} = \frac{(3\times 10^{8})^{2}}{(1.5\times 10^{8})^{2}} = 4.\] With \(\mu_{r} = 2\), \(\varepsilon_{r} = 2\). The correct choice is D.
authoredSolutions.6: Reflection, diffraction, interference and polarisation are all accounted for by treating light as a wave. The photoelectric effect, however, requires light to deliver energy in discrete quanta \(h\nu\); a wave picture predicts a threshold-free, intensity-dependent emission that is not observed. So only statement (C) fails, and the correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.7: Least count \(= \dfrac{\text{pitch}}{\text{no. of circular divisions}} = \dfrac{1}{100} = 0.01\text{ mm}\). \[d = \text{MSR} + (\text{CSR})(\text{LC}) = 1 + 42(0.01) = 1.42\text{ mm}.\] Setting \(1.42 = x/50\) gives \(x = 71\), so the correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.8: Take a pillbox straddling the shell. Only the outward face carries flux (the field inside a charged conducting shell is zero), so \(E\,dA = \dfrac{\sigma\,dA}{\varepsilon_{0}}\), giving \[E = \frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_{0}}.\] The correct choice is C. (The value \(\sigma/2\varepsilon_{0}\) belongs to a non-conducting sheet, not to the surface of a shell.)
authoredSolutions.9: The potential difference between \(B\) and \(D\) vanishes when the bridge is balanced. Reduce each arm first: arm \(AB\) is \(24\,\Omega\) in parallel with two \(12\,\Omega\) in series, i.e. \(24\|24 = 12\,\Omega\); arm \(BC\) is \(1\,\Omega\|1\,\Omega = 0.5\,\Omega\); arm \(CD\) is \(0.5\,\Omega\); arm \(AD\) is \(x\) in series with \(12\,\Omega\|12\,\Omega = 6\,\Omega\), i.e. \(x+6\). Balance requires \[\frac{R_{AB}}{R_{AD}} = \frac{R_{BC}}{R_{CD}} \Rightarrow \frac{12}{x+6} = \frac{0.5}{0.5} = 1,\] so \(x = 6\,\Omega\) and the correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.10: First law: \(C\,dT = C_{V}\,dT + P\,dV\). For the given gas \(PV^{2} = RT\); differentiating at constant \(P\), \[P\,d(V^{2}) = R\,dT \Rightarrow 2PV\,dV = R\,dT \Rightarrow P\,dV = \frac{R\,dT}{2V}.\] Substituting, \(C_{P} = C_{V} + \dfrac{R}{2V}\). The correct choice is D.
authoredSolutions.11: Torque \(= \vec{r}\times\vec{F}\Rightarrow [M L^{2} T^{-2}]\), which is IV. Magnetic field from \(F = qvB\Rightarrow B = \dfrac{MLT^{-2}}{(AT)(LT^{-1})} = [M T^{-2} A^{-1}]\), which is III. Magnetic moment \(= IA \Rightarrow [L^{2}A]\), which is II. From \(B = \dfrac{\mu_{0}}{4\pi}\dfrac{I\,dl}{r^{2}}\), \(\mu_{0} = \dfrac{Br^{2}}{I\,dl} = [M L T^{-2} A^{-2}]\), which is I. Hence A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I and the correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.12: In a series LCR circuit \(I = \dfrac{V}{\sqrt{R^{2} + (X_{L}-X_{C})^{2}}}\). At resonance \(X_{L} = X_{C}\), the impedance is minimum \((=R)\) and the current is maximum, so Statement I is true. For the same source and the same \(R\), a purely resistive circuit carries \(V/R\), which is the largest current the LCR circuit can ever reach (it attains it only at resonance). So the resistive-circuit current can never be smaller, and Statement II is also true. The correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.13: From the circuit, \(A\) is inverted and fed to one input of the OR gate, while the AND of \(A\) and \(B\) is fed to the other. Hence \[Y = \bar{A} + A\cdot B = \bar{A} + B.\] Evaluating: \((A,B)=(0,0)\Rightarrow Y=1\); \((0,1)\Rightarrow Y=1\); \((1,0)\Rightarrow Y=0\); \((1,1)\Rightarrow Y=1\). The table reading \(Y = 1,1,0,1\) is option B.
authoredSolutions.14: Both gases in the same sample share one temperature, and \(v_{rms} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}}\), so \(v_{rms}\propto 1/\sqrt{M}\). Therefore \[\frac{v_{He}}{v_{O_{2}}} = \sqrt{\frac{M_{O_{2}}}{M_{He}}} = \sqrt{\frac{32}{4}} = 2\sqrt{2}.\] The ratio is \(2\sqrt{2}:1\), so the correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.15: For an Atwood machine \(a = \dfrac{(m_{2}-m_{1})g}{m_{1}+m_{2}}\). Setting \(a = g/\sqrt{2}\), \[\frac{m_{2}-m_{1}}{m_{2}+m_{1}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}.\] Writing \(k = m_{1}/m_{2}\): \(\sqrt{2}(1-k) = 1+k\Rightarrow k(\sqrt{2}+1) = \sqrt{2}-1\), so \[\frac{m_{1}}{m_{2}} = \frac{\sqrt{2}-1}{\sqrt{2}+1}.\] The correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.16: With momentum fixed, \(K = \dfrac{p^{2}}{2m}\), so \(K\propto 1/m\). The smallest mass \(m/2\), particle A, therefore has the largest kinetic energy. The option naming particle A is C.
authoredSolutions.17: During the acceleration phase the average speed is \(\dfrac{0+80}{2} = 40\) km/h, covering \(40t\); during the constant phase it covers \(80(3t) = 240t\). Total distance \(= 280t\) over total time \(4t\), so \[\bar{v} = \frac{280t}{4t} = 70\text{ km/h}.\] The correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.18: The current element lies along \(\hat{i}\) and the field point lies on the \(y\)-axis, so \(\theta = 90^{\circ}\) and \(\sin\theta = 1\). By the Biot-Savart law \[B = \frac{\mu_{0}}{4\pi}\frac{I\,\Delta l\,\sin\theta}{r^{2}} = 10^{-7}\times\frac{10\times 0.01}{(0.5)^{2}} = 10^{-7}\times 0.4 = 4\times 10^{-8}\text{ T}.\] The correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.19: At terminal velocity the acceleration is zero, so weight balances buoyancy plus viscous drag: \(mg = F_{B} + F_{v}\). The displaced volume is \(V = m/\rho\), so \(F_{B} = \dfrac{m}{\rho}\rho_{0}g\). Hence \[F_{v} = mg - \frac{m\rho_{0}g}{\rho} = mg\left(1 - \frac{\rho_{0}}{\rho}\right).\] The correct choice is D.
authoredSolutions.20: Einstein's photoelectric equation gives \(eV_{s} = E - \phi\), so \[\phi = 2.48\text{ eV} - 0.5\text{ eV} = 1.98\text{ eV}.\] The correct choice is D.
authoredSolutions.21: No external torque acts, so angular momentum is conserved: \(I_{1}\omega_{1} = I_{2}\omega_{2}\). For a uniform sphere \(I = \tfrac{2}{5}MR^{2}\) with \(M\) unchanged, so \[\frac{2}{5}MR^{2}\frac{2\pi}{T_{1}} = \frac{2}{5}M\left(\frac{3R}{4}\right)^{2}\frac{2\pi}{T_{2}} \Rightarrow T_{2} = \left(\frac{3}{4}\right)^{2}T_{1}.\] Thus \(T_{2} = \dfrac{9}{16}\times 24 = 13.5\) hours, i.e. 13 hours 30 minutes, so the blank is \(13\).
authoredSolutions.22: Each infinite sheet produces a uniform field \(\dfrac{|\sigma|}{2\varepsilon_{0}}\), directed away from a positive sheet and towards a negative one. The point \(P\) lies between \(x=a\) and \(x=3a\). The sheet \(-\sigma\) at \(x=-a\) pulls the field towards \(-\hat{i}\) with \(\dfrac{\sigma}{2\varepsilon_{0}}\); the sheet \(-2\sigma\) at \(x=a\) also gives \(-\hat{i}\) with \(\dfrac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_{0}}\); the sheet \(+\sigma\) at \(x=3a\) pushes away from itself, again \(-\hat{i}\), with \(\dfrac{\sigma}{2\varepsilon_{0}}\). Adding, \[\vec{E}_{P} = -\left(\frac{\sigma}{2\varepsilon_{0}} + \frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_{0}} + \frac{\sigma}{2\varepsilon_{0}}\right)\hat{i} = -\frac{2\sigma}{\varepsilon_{0}}\hat{i}.\] The magnitude is \(\dfrac{2\sigma}{\varepsilon_{0}}\), so \(x = 2\).
authoredSolutions.23: Volume is conserved: \(1000\cdot\tfrac{4}{3}\pi r^{3} = \tfrac{4}{3}\pi R^{3}\Rightarrow R = 10r\). Surface energy is \(T\) times area, so \[\frac{E_{1000}}{E_{\text{big}}} = \frac{1000(4\pi r^{2})T}{4\pi R^{2}T} = \frac{1000r^{2}}{100r^{2}} = 10.\] Comparing with \(\dfrac{10}{x}\) gives \(x = 1\).
authoredSolutions.24: A dc source sees only the coil's resistance: \(R = \dfrac{100}{5} = 20\,\Omega\). With ac, \[Z = \sqrt{R^{2}+X_{L}^{2}} = \sqrt{400 + (20\sqrt{3})^{2}} = \sqrt{400+1200} = 40\,\Omega.\] With \(V_{rms} = \dfrac{200}{\sqrt{2}}\), \(I_{rms} = \dfrac{200/\sqrt{2}}{40}\) so \(I_{rms}^{2} = 12.5\,A^{2}\). Only the resistance dissipates power: \[P = I_{rms}^{2}R = 12.5\times 20 = 250\text{ W}.\]
authoredSolutions.25: At minimum deviation \(r_{1}=r_{2}=A/2\) and \(\mu = \dfrac{\sin\!\left(\frac{A+\delta_{m}}{2}\right)}{\sin\!\left(\frac{A}{2}\right)}\). Given \(\delta_{m} = A\), \[\mu = \frac{\sin A}{\sin(A/2)} = \frac{2\sin(A/2)\cos(A/2)}{\sin(A/2)} = 2\cos\frac{A}{2}.\] So \(2\cos(A/2) = \sqrt{3}\Rightarrow \cos(A/2) = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\Rightarrow A/2 = 30^{\circ}\), giving \(A = 60^{\circ}\).
authoredSolutions.26: Stretching conserves volume: \(\pi r^{2}l = \pi\left(\dfrac{r}{2}\right)^{2}l' \Rightarrow l' = 4l\). Since \(R = \dfrac{\rho l}{A}\), \[\frac{R'}{R} = \frac{l'}{l}\cdot\frac{A}{A'} = 4\times 4 = 16.\] Hence \(x = 16\).
authoredSolutions.27: For hydrogen \(r_{n} = a_{0}n^{2}\), so \[n^{2} = \frac{8.48}{0.529} = 16 \Rightarrow n = 4.\] Since \(E_{n} = \dfrac{E}{n^{2}}\), the energy is \(\dfrac{E}{16}\) and \(x = 16\).

authoredSolutions.29: The maximum speed in SHM occurs at the mean position: \[v_{\max} = A\omega = A\frac{2\pi}{T} = 0.06\times\frac{2\pi}{\pi} = 0.12\text{ m/s} = 12\text{ cm/s}.\]

authoredSolutions.92: Helium is monatomic, \(C_{V} = \tfrac{3}{2}R\). By the first law \(\Delta Q = nC_{V}\Delta T + W\): \[48 = (1)\left(\frac{3}{2}\times 8.3\right)(2) + W = 24.9 + W,\] so \(W = 23.1\text{ J}\) and the correct choice is D.
authoredSolutions.93: With 20 main-scale divisions per cm, \(1\text{ MSD} = 0.05\text{ cm}\), and \(1\text{ VSD} = \tfrac{49}{50}\text{ MSD}\), so \[\text{LC} = 1\text{ MSD} - 1\text{ VSD} = \frac{0.05}{50} = 0.001\text{ cm}.\] The three readings are \(8.45+26(0.001) = 8.476\text{ cm}\) (mark on paper), \(7.12+41(0.001) = 7.161\text{ cm}\) (mark seen through the slab) and \(4.05+1(0.001) = 4.051\text{ cm}\) (top surface). authoredSolutions.94: The intensity of an electromagnetic wave is \[I = \frac{1}{2}\varepsilon_{0}E_{0}^{2}c = \frac{1}{2}\times 9\times 10^{-12}\times(600)^{2}\times 3\times 10^{8}.\] Evaluating, \(\tfrac{1}{2}\times 9\times 36\times 3 = 486\ W/m^{2}\). The correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.95: Inside a uniform sphere \(g_{d} = g\left(1-\dfrac{d}{R}\right)\). With \(d = R/4\), \(g_{d} = \tfrac{3}{4}g\). The mass is unchanged, so the weight becomes \[W_{d} = \frac{3}{4}\times 300 = 225\text{ N}.\] The correct choice is D.
authoredSolutions.96: A photon can create a hole only if its energy is at least the acceptor-level energy, so the longest usable wavelength satisfies \(E = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda}\): \[\lambda_{\max} = \frac{1242\ eV\,nm}{6\ eV} = 207\text{ nm}.\] The correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.97: For a banked road with friction the maximum safe speed is \[v_{\max} = \sqrt{rg\left(\frac{\tan\theta + \mu}{1-\mu\tan\theta}\right)}.\] With \(\tan 30^{\circ} = 1/1.73 = 0.578\), \[v_{\max} = \sqrt{300\times 10\times\frac{0.578+0.2}{1-0.2(0.578)}} = \sqrt{3000\times 0.880} = 51.4\text{ m/s}.\] The mass is irrelevant. authoredSolutions.98: Identical conductors in contact share charge equally. After \(R\) touches \(P\): both carry \(Q/2\). Then \(R\) (holding \(Q/2\)) touches \(S\) (holding \(Q\)): each becomes \(\dfrac{Q/2 + Q}{2} = \dfrac{3Q}{4}\). Since \(F\propto q_{1}q_{2}\), \[F' = F\times\frac{(Q/2)(3Q/4)}{Q^{2}} = \frac{3}{8}\times 16 = 6\text{ N}.\] The correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.99: The magnitude of the self-induced emf is \(|\varepsilon| = L\left|\dfrac{di}{dt}\right|\). Here \(\Delta i = 2-(-2) = 4\text{ A}\) in \(0.2\text{ s}\), so \[0.1 = L\times\frac{4}{0.2} = 20L \Rightarrow L = 5\times 10^{-3}\text{ H} = 5\text{ mH}.\] The correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.100: For a biconvex lens \(R_{1} = +15\text{ cm}\) and \(R_{2} = -30\text{ cm}\). The lensmaker's formula gives \[\frac{1}{20} = (\mu-1)\left(\frac{1}{15}-\frac{1}{-30}\right) = (\mu-1)\frac{3}{30}.\] So \(\mu - 1 = \dfrac{1}{2}\) and \(\mu = 1.5\). The correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.101: A non-rigid (vibrating) diatomic molecule has \(f = 3 + 2 + 2 = 7\) degrees of freedom (3 translational, 2 rotational, 2 vibrational). authoredSolutions.102: The chain plus the hanging body is in equilibrium, so the branch must support the total weight: \[T = 200 + (10)(10) = 300\text{ N}.\] The correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.103: The photon energy is \(E = \dfrac{1240}{300} = 4.13\text{ eV}\). Then \[eV_{s} = E - \phi = 4.13 - 2.13 = 2.0\text{ eV},\] so the stopping potential is \(2\text{ V}\). The correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.104: The filament current is \(I = \dfrac{P}{V} = \dfrac{110}{220} = 0.5\text{ A}\). Since \(I = \dfrac{ne}{t}\), \[\frac{n}{t} = \frac{0.5}{1.6\times 10^{-19}} = 3.125\times 10^{18} = 31.25\times 10^{17}\text{ per second}.\] The correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.105: Since \(p = \sqrt{2mK}\), \(p\propto\sqrt{K}\). If \(K_{f} = 36K_{i}\) then \(p_{f} = 6p_{i}\), so \[\%\text{ increase} = \frac{6p_{i}-p_{i}}{p_{i}}\times 100 = 500\%.\] The correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.106: A soap bubble has two liquid-air surfaces, so the excess pressure is twice that of a single drop: \[\Delta P = 2\left(\frac{2S}{R}\right) = \frac{4S}{R}.\] The correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.107: (A) The magnetic susceptibility of a para- or diamagnetic material is a constant independent of the magnetising field, giving the horizontal line III.
